name: app.moosetracker/moose-tracker
title: Moose Tracker
description: Synth, sampler and music tracker for AI assistants: sound effects, UI sounds and songs as audio.

tools.name: describe
tools.description: Use this when the user asks for a sound effect, click, notification, jingle, audio, music, song or soundtrack, or mentions Moose Tracker: returns usage notes. No arguments gives a short index (workflow, limits, formats, next steps); topic opens one section: syntax, limits, styles, recipes, presets, mtl, instrument, effects, modulation, drums, loops, formats, sfx, examples, errors, genres, generators, samples, search, not_supported, workflow, volume, mix, sounds, character, photos; q searches presets and the sample library; with topic="syntax", q opens one syntax section (q="arp") or a field. Song text up to 1024 KB; one audio file holds about 5 min as WAV, longer as Ogg or Opus (exact seconds per format in the index). Tool list 1.7.2. Schema 0479948e.

q.description: Search word, example id, role for topic=instrument; for samples also category=X genre=Y

category.description: topic=samples: only this category (drums, keys, pads, ...)

genre.description: topic=samples: only packs for this genre

tools.name: sfx
tools.description: Produces sound-effect files (up to 16 per call) to embed in an app, game, UI or video. Each item is one of: a role (press, release, toggle_on, toggle_off, continuous_tick, success, warning, notify, complete) with a shared family (seed, character, root, scale) for a coherent UI set with playback hints; a recipe (describe topic=recipes; recipes are starting points) tailored with pitch, bright, dur and seed, pairs alike; or an instrument line with play, which auditions one designed voice. Kinds mix in one call. revise patches a family by its handle. Reports design_mode and loudness; WAV by default, Ogg or Opus on request. Files last 2 h; https://moosetracker.app/acceptable-use.html Schema 0479948e.

mtl.description: Custom effect as a tiny MTL song (<= 2048 bytes)

instrument.description: Audition one voice: text after iN, e.g. - wave=saw cutoff=45 or sample "upright-bass" (describe topic=instrument)

play.description: Notes for instrument: C3 E3, chord C3+E3, C3:4 = 4 beats, . = rest

pitch.description: Semitones; 12 = octave. Lower is heavier, higher lighter

seed.description: 0 = plain recipe; others shift pitch, length and tone repeatably (reproducible, not unique)

dur.description: Length in seconds, fitted within 8% or 30 ms

format.description: Default wav; ogg = Vorbis 44.1 kHz; opus = Ogg Opus 48 kHz

tools.name: research_composition
tools.description: Finds composition advice. brief: once when starting a real song (sections, over ~20 s), not for simple sounds: advice with ranges for every stage (plan, harmony, melody, layers, sound, mix, review) from a curated corpus of about 50 styles; stage picks one, limit and avoid page. Then song(plan). q: before writing a melody, harmony, bass line, groove or arrangement, look up the music-theory guide (principle, MTL example, common mistakes; idioms for every genre id), e.g. q="melody feels static"; ids fetches entries song checks cite. Advice is retrieved: no AI composes music here. Schema 0479948e.

key.description: With q: e.g. F#m, D dorian

stage.description: Omit for all stages at once

tools.name: lyrics
tools.description: Analyzes lyric text for setting to music: each word's syllables, stress and phones (ARPAbet), the rhyme scheme with perfect and near rhymes, scansion against a poetic meter, and where each syllable can start on a tracker rhythm grid for a time signature (stressed syllables on strong beats, a pickup for an unstressed start), with warnings for lines that do not scan. EXPERIMENTAL: the singing voice and lyric setting are early features; word clarity and fit vary from song to song, so render and listen before relying on a result. It writes no melody and no words of its own (fit mode only reshapes a melody you send): the assistant writes the notes, then puts each syllable on its note in MTL (C4'twin- D4'kle; '_ holds a syllable over more notes). Word setting: mode=plan returns, for every line, exactly how many notes it needs and their lengths as a melody template (x:2 x:2 x:4: write the tune on that rhythm); mode=fit with melody checks and fits the words on a melody you wrote, adapting it (adapt, default true): extra syllables split a note (split=repeat repeats the pitch, pass steps toward the next note), a line that starts unstressed on the downbeat gets a pickup note, extra notes carry the syllable (melisma '_), and the last note is held to its bar line (hold); every change is listed, and warnings name syllables that are crammed, stress-inverted or off the beat and phrases that are shorter or longer than the bars (bars). Each fit line returns a ready MTL cell string and the adapted melody. Pronunciation comes from the dictionary; words guessed by rule are listed (fix with say). melody: one line per lyric line (a "\n" between lines, or an array). Tokens split by spaces: a pitch (C5, F#4, Bb3; octave 0-9, C4 = 48), optionally with its length in rows (C5:4; default = step rows); "." a rest of one step, ".3" three steps, ".3r" three rows; "x" a placeholder pitch (from plan mode: x:2); "@-2" first token only: the line starts at row -2 (a pickup before the bar; default 0). A note lasts until the next token. Example: "C5 D5 E5:4 . G5:2". Up to 48 lines per call. Schema 0479948e.

text.description: The lyrics, one sung line per line

meter.description: Poetic meter to scan against; auto picks the best fit

rpb.description: Rows per beat (quarter note) of the pattern, default 4

bars.description: Bars per line; omitted, one count that suits every line

bpm.description: Tempo, for the shortest singable syllable (default 100)

pickup.description: Allow unstressed syllables before the bar (default true)

say.description: Pronunciations for names or invented words, ARPAbet with stress: {"kurtis":"K ER1 T IH0 S"}

detail.description: full adds phones and meter notes to the text

mode.description: analyze (default): grid rows only. plan: notes and rhythm each line needs (write the melody second). fit: put the words on melody (default when melody is sent)

melody.description: With fit: one melody line per lyric line, e.g. "C5 D5 E5:4 . G5:2" (pitch[:rows], . rest, x placeholder, @-2 pickup start)

step.description: Rows per melody token without a length (default rpb/2, an eighth note)

adapt.description: fit: change the melody to suit the words (split, pickup, melisma); false only reports (default true)

hold.description: fit: hold the last note of a line to its bar line (default true)

split.description: fit: pitch of a note split in two: repeat it, or step toward the next note (default repeat)

tools.name: song
tools.description: Plans and analyzes a song written in MTL text (render checks too); returns a share link that plays it in the browser (90 days, no render). Stages: plan, write, light analysis loop, one deep analysis, fix; then the share link to listen; one render only when the user asks for an audio file. song(plan) gives a skeleton; analyze:true: light (repeatable); deep:true: measured (once). Your own sound: i3 - name="Glass Lead" wave=saw cutoff=55 (a quoted word after iN is a preset); tracks play it as i3. The syntax: describe(topic="syntax") gives the core grammar and a list of sections, each read with q (q="synth" every synth field, q="arp", q="modulation" ...). Stopping a note: = releases it (its release plays out); an ECx effect cuts it dead after x ticks (_!EC0 on that step, D4!EC3 on the note). A sung song can also become a Singalong video (present with singalong); offer it when it fits, such as a song for someone's birthday or a thank-you. Each reply has a songId: send ref instead of the text again, with layers for batch edits (tracks, instruments, mix, order). It warns when a song is longer than one audio file holds (WAV about 5 min, Ogg or Opus longer). To work on a song in another program, convert it to MIDI or a tracker module. Schema 0479948e.

mtl.description: Song in MTL text (describe topic=mtl). Kept 2 hours as a working copy: later calls can send ref (the songId) instead.

ref.description: Instead of mtl: a songId from an earlier reply (kept 2 hours), a render asset id, or a share link

compose.description: Instead of mtl: {bpm, form, chords, parts:[{id,gen}]}. describe(topic="generators")

genre.description: Scores against this genre's factors (each genre scores its own); describe(topic="genres")

analyze.description: Light analysis: no audio, instant, free. Suited to every edit

range.description: With analyze: one section, e.g. "2" or "2-3" (order entries)

compare.description: With analyze: A/B against an earlier songId, asset id or share link

deep.description: With analyze: deep analysis, a measured analysis-only render. Suited to once or twice when the song is nearly done

alts.description: Other MTL versions to rank by score

melody.description: Melody track, if not the highest

keep.description: Kept on purpose, with a reason: flag codes {"POLY.CUT": "mono arp"} ("POLY.CUT:3" one track) or score codes (REPEAT, LEN...), not deducted

plan.description: Alone: {bpm, meter, key, peak, sections:[{id, bars, energy 1-5, role}], mix?} gives a skeleton, timing, checks

skip_plan.description: Reason to skip research and plan for a full song (else they come first)

layers.description: With mtl or ref: batch edits {add:["A: 3 i3 v40: C4 . . ."], replace, remove:["A:3"], instruments, mix, notes, order}; returns the edited song

notes.description: Polyphony: [{ch, ins, section?, notes:[[pitch, startBeat, beats, vel]]}]; placed on sub-channels; vel 0-64 as vNN

mix.description: dB; "-inf" silences, 0 resets. Faders balance (first choice), gain sets one sound, level is overall loudness

order.description: The song's order line, e.g. "A B C D C D" (| marks the loop start)

energy.description: Planned 1-5 per order entry, for check:true

tools.name: render
tools.description: Produces WAV, Ogg or Opus files: the audio file a user asks for, to download or to embed in a game, app, presentation or video. When the user wants to hear a song, a tune or music, please give them song's share link instead of a file: it plays straight away in the browser, costs no render, lasts 90 days, and the Moose Tracker web app it opens exports WAV or Ogg of any length on their own device. A render is for an audio file that goes into something else, and each one counts against the hourly render quota. Send mtl, ref (a songId) or compose; it checks the song itself (syntax: describe(topic="syntax"), sections by q). One file holds up to 5 min as WAV and up to 10 min as Ogg or Opus; a longer request is refused with the exact limit. len gives exact seconds; loop:true adds seamless loop points; stems:true gives one file per instrument role (@lead, @bass, @drums...); adaptive:true gives a zip of same-length looping layers in intensities, stingers from extra cues, a manifest, a Web Audio player and Godot, Unity, FMOD and Wwise notes; cues renders named sections. A long render replies rendering with asset ids, and assets(ids) gives the links when done; a client with MCP Tasks gets a task instead, which completes with the links, so the agent can carry on meanwhile. Files last 2 h; https://moosetracker.app/acceptable-use.html Schema 0479948e.

mtl.description: Song in MTL text (describe topic=mtl). Kept 2 hours as a working copy: later calls can send ref (the songId) instead.

ref.description: Instead of mtl: a songId from an earlier reply (kept 2 hours), a render asset id, or a share link

compose.description: Instead of mtl: {bpm, form, chords, parts:[{id,gen}]}. describe(topic="generators")

skip_review.description: Reason to skip a full song's deep review (else it comes first)

format.description: Default wav; ogg = Vorbis 44.1 kHz; opus = Ogg Opus 48 kHz

detail.description: Adds score, per-section loudness and MIX flags with fixes

audition.description: Hear one channel alone as a preview; try swaps its sound: {ch:3, try:"i3 \"Warm Pad\""}

levels.description: Your own intensities in order, each a list of roles: {"explore":["pad"],"fight":["pad","bass","drums","lead"]}

adaptive.description: A zip of same-length looping layers grouped into intensities (default calm, tense, full; set your own with adaptive.levels), stingers from extra cues, manifest.json, a Web Audio player and setup notes for Godot, Unity, FMOD and Wwise (describe topic=loops)

len.description: Exact seconds: a short song repeats its order (said in the result), a long one fades out; never silence

preview.description: One section (range, default 1), ≤20 s Opus, light quota, MIX flags

tools.name: convert
tools.description: Use this when a song should move between MTL text, a Moose Tracker .mtk project, a share link and standard files: MIDI (.mid, type 0 or 1) and MOD, XM, S3M or IT tracker modules, in either direction, or sheet music: in from MusicXML (.musicxml/.xml), compressed MusicXML (.mxl), ABC notation, or a PDF that has the MusicXML or MIDI attached, and out to MusicXML 4.0 (to musicxml, for MuseScore, Dorico, Finale or Sibelius; key and time override the inferred key and the song's time signature; layout full (every part), voice-piano (the vocal line with lyrics and chord symbols over a grand-staff piano) or lead-sheet (the melody with lyrics and chord symbols; diagrams adds guitar chord boxes); parts sets a part off or on 1 or 2 staves by its key, listed in the reply's notes; to pdf or svg: a link that opens the song in the web app with the engraved PDF/SVG export ready). Files come in as base64 in input (MusicXML and ABC also as plain text) or as an https address in url; from file works the type out. An import to mtl returns the MTL plus a share link (or the .mtk as a download when the song is long); a written file comes back as a download link; describe topic=formats. It takes a song into another program (a DAW, a notation app, another tracker) or brings one in; voices maps channels to sample packs or presets on import, and feel adds swing or humanize. Cues and macros are compiled away in .mtk and share links. from photo reads a photo or scan of printed sheet music (optical music recognition with homr, run on the user's own computer; describe topic=photos): the photo comes as photo (a file attached in ChatGPT), url, base64 input, upload (the job id from the scan link or upload card) or path (a file on the user's computer, with the moosetracker-mcp package), and the import returns a draft song plus the bars to compare with the photo. Schema 0479948e.

input.description: The song, .mtk JSON or share link; for a file, the file as base64 (up to about 700 KB; MusicXML and ABC may be plain text). Omit when url is given

url.description: Instead of input: a public https address of the file (up to about 700 KB)

name.description: The file's name, e.g. tune.mxl (helps from file tell the type)

photo.description: from photo: the photo of the sheet music as a file attached in the chat (ChatGPT fills this in)

upload.description: from photo: the job id of a photo uploaded with the scan link or the upload card

path.description: from photo: the photo's full path on the user's computer (read by the moosetracker-mcp package there)

key.description: to musicxml: the key, e.g. "Eb major", "F# minor" (default: worked out from the notes)

time.description: to musicxml: time signature, e.g. "3/4", "6/8" (default: the song's)

layout.description: to musicxml, pdf or svg: full score (default), voice and piano, or lead sheet

parts.description: to musicxml: per part key ("3" = channel 3, "4d" = the drums of channel 4): "off", or "1" or "2" staves

chords.description: to musicxml, pdf or svg: chord symbols from the harmony (default: on for voice-piano and lead-sheet, and for full scores with a chordal part)

diagrams.description: to musicxml, pdf or svg: guitar chord diagrams with the chord symbols

bassFill.description: to musicxml, pdf or svg: a piano with nothing for the left hand plays the bass part there (default: on for voice-piano)

tools.name: present
tools.description: Hands songs to the user to listen to: the finished song to enjoy (mode listen), examples to choose between (choose), or two versions to compare at the same playback position (ab). Where the chat app shows cards, a player plays them on the user's device with Moose Tracker's own engine, and its Download opens the song in the web app, which exports WAV or Ogg of any length on the user's computer; elsewhere the reply gives each song's share link. Use it when the song is ready for the user, not for checks, auditions or previews. Nothing is rendered in the cloud and it counts against no render quota. singalong (KUR-330) adds a bouncing-ball lyrics card for a sung song: a little moose hops syllable to syllable over the words while it plays, and Make video saves a WebM (VP9 + Opus) in 16:9, 9:16 or 1:1, light or dark, encoded on the user's device. The reply gives assetId: after the user makes the video, assets([assetId]) returns its download link (2 h) to attach in chat or email. Shown words: describe(topic="syntax", q="voice"). When you need the video file itself (to embed it, or to send it to someone), you must present it with mode:"review": the card shows the user the video to check, Accept sends you its download link (and assets([assetId]) returns it), Request changes sends you their notes to revise and present again. The MCP never sends anything: deliver it with your own messaging tools. Mode scan instead shows an upload button for a photo of sheet music (upload: the job id convert from photo gave), for chat apps that cannot pass an image to a tool. When it fits (a song with words, a teaching or classroom song, a party song, or a song made for someone: a birthday, a thank-you, get well, a greeting), you might offer a Singalong video, the words with a little moose hopping along, like a musical greeting card they can send. Offer it as an option; don't make one unasked. Schema 0479948e.

items.description: The songs, in the order to show them

ref.description: The songId from the song reply (a share link or render asset id also works; a long link copied by hand can get damaged)

mtl.description: Instead of ref: the song text

label.description: What the user sees, e.g. "A: brighter mix"

mode.description: listen: one finished song; choose: examples to pick from; ab: two versions; review: one sung song as a singalong video for the user to check (Accept gives you its link, Request changes their notes); scan: a photo upload button (no items). Default: listen for one item, ab for two, choose for more

upload.description: mode scan: the job id from convert from photo

aspect.description: 16:9 landscape (1280x720), 9:16 portrait for phones and stories (720x1280), 1:1 square (720x720)

format.description: webm (VP9 + Opus) is the default: leave it out. mp4 (H.264 + AAC) only when the user asks for an MP4. A device that can't make the one asked for makes the other

singalong.description: A sung song (a wave=voice lead with 'syl syllables): the card shows the words with a moose bouncing on each syllable, and its Make video saves a singalong video made on the user's device; the reply gives the assetId assets() fetches it with once the user has made it. listen mode, one item

tools.name: assets
tools.description: Use this when a download link was lost or is about to expire, or a render replied rendering: pass the asset ids from the result to get the links or the status, with no re-render and no charge. Files live about 2 h; verify:true re-checks a file's hash. An id that has expired says so: the same request again returns the same files (the synthesizer is deterministic). Schema 0479948e.

tools.name: feedback
tools.description: Sends a note to the Moose Tracker team about a bug, a confusing tool, or a missing feature. Up to 20000 characters per call; longer reports can be split into parts. Notes are kept 1 year; include what happened, the call and its reply. Schema 0479948e.

message.description: What happened or what is needed; no personal details. Up to 20000 characters; longer reports go in parts (ref, part, parts).

mtl.description: Optional: the song or sound involved, only if relevant

ref.description: Optional label shared by every part of one long report; parts with the same ref count as one submission
